chunks: And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: I did not hesitate in anything that I am to do as I hesitate in taking the soul of My believing servant, because I love to meet him while he dislikes death; so I conceal it from him. And if there were on the earth only one believer, he would suffice for Me instead of all My creation, and I would make for him from his faith a companion so that he would not need anyone in it.
ai.seo_question: Why does Allah hesitate to take the soul of a believer?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi from *Kitab al-Mumin* elucidates the divine attribute of *taraddud* (deliberate hesitation) specifically regarding the death of believers, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the spiritual nobility of the soul's transition. The statement 'I sufficed with him' underscores the ontological weight of a single believer's faith, suggesting that the believer's inner state is so pure it can serve as a sufficient companion (*ansa*) to the Divine, mitigating the need for external creation. This concept is often linked by scholars to the idea that the believer's heart becomes a throne for God's presence, making their individual existence a microcosm of the entire universe.
